description: ALB − TP per patient is the mean of the per-test differences.

c.request: Linking lab records to patients by `ID` (dropping unmatched lab records), work out each patient's (`ID`, `SEX`) average `ALB` − `TP` and average `APTT` − `PT`, then average these within each sex (every `SEX` value, blank or missing included, as its own group). Keep the sexes whose average `APTT` − `PT` is above the mean of the sex-level `APTT` − `PT` averages. Give a single row averaging, across those sexes: the `ALB` − `TP` figure, the `APTT` − `PT` figure, and how far the `APTT` − `PT` figure exceeds that mean. Averages ignore missing values; don't round. ALB − TP per patient is the mean of the per-test differences.
c.sql:
WITH patient_averages AS (
    SELECT
        p.ID,
        p.SEX,
        AVG(l.ALB - l.TP) AS avg_alb_minus_tp,
        AVG(l.APTT - l.PT) AS avg_aptt_minus_pt
    FROM Patient AS p
    JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID
    GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX
),
sex_averages AS (
    SELECT
        SEX,
        AVG(avg_alb_minus_tp) AS avg_alb_minus_tp,
        AVG(avg_aptt_minus_pt) AS avg_aptt_minus_pt
    FROM patient_averages
    GROUP BY SEX
),
sex_mean AS (
    SELECT AVG(avg_aptt_minus_pt) AS mean_aptt_minus_pt
    FROM sex_averages
)
SELECT
    AVG(s.avg_alb_minus_tp) AS avg_alb_minus_tp,
    AVG(s.avg_aptt_minus_pt) AS avg_aptt_minus_pt,
    AVG(s.avg_aptt_minus_pt - m.mean_aptt_minus_pt) AS avg_excess_aptt_minus_pt
FROM sex_averages AS s
CROSS JOIN sex_mean AS m
WHERE s.avg_aptt_minus_pt > m.mean_aptt_minus_pt;

b.request: For each matched patient, average the nonmissing per-test differences `ALB − TP` and `APTT − PT`; then average those patient-level figures by `SEX`, treating each distinct value (including blank or missing) as a group. Select sexes whose average `APTT − PT` exceeds the mean across all sex-level `APTT − PT` averages, and return one row with the unweighted averages across selected sexes of their `ALB − TP` averages, their `APTT − PT` averages, and each selected sex’s excess over that mean; ignore missing values and do not round
b.sql:
WITH per_test AS (
    SELECT p.ID, p.SEX,
           l.ALB - l.TP AS alb_tp_diff,
           l.APTT - l.PT AS aptt_pt_diff
    FROM Patient AS p
    JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID
), patient_avgs AS (
    SELECT ID, SEX,
           AVG(alb_tp_diff) AS alb_tp_avg,
           AVG(aptt_pt_diff) AS aptt_pt_avg
    FROM per_test
    GROUP BY ID, SEX
), sex_avgs AS (
    SELECT SEX,
           AVG(alb_tp_avg) AS alb_tp_avg,
           AVG(aptt_pt_avg) AS aptt_pt_avg
    FROM patient_avgs
    GROUP BY SEX
), sex_mean AS (
    SELECT AVG(aptt_pt_avg) AS mean_aptt_pt_avg
    FROM sex_avgs
), selected AS (
    SELECT s.alb_tp_avg, s.aptt_pt_avg,
           s.aptt_pt_avg - m.mean_aptt_pt_avg AS excess
    FROM sex_avgs AS s
    CROSS JOIN sex_mean AS m
    WHERE s.aptt_pt_avg > m.mean_aptt_pt_avg
)
SELECT AVG(alb_tp_avg) AS avg_alb_minus_tp,
       AVG(aptt_pt_avg) AS avg_aptt_minus_pt,
       AVG(excess) AS avg_excess_over_sex_mean
FROM selected;

a.request: Linking lab records to patients by `ID` (dropping unmatched lab records), for each patient (`ID`, `SEX`) compute the average per-test difference `ALB` − `TP` (using only tests where both are present) and the average per-test difference `APTT` − `PT`. Average these patient figures within each sex (every `SEX` value, blank or missing included, as its own group). Keep the sexes whose average `APTT` − `PT` is above the mean of the sex-level `APTT` − `PT` averages. Give a single row averaging, across those sexes: the `ALB` − `TP` figure, the `APTT` − `PT` figure, and how far the `APTT` − `PT` figure exceeds that mean. Averages ignore missing values; don't round.
a.sql:
WITH patient_averages AS (
    SELECT
        p.ID,
        p.SEX,
        AVG(CASE WHEN l.ALB IS NOT NULL AND l.TP IS NOT NULL THEN l.ALB - l.TP END) AS avg_alb_minus_tp,
        AVG(CASE WHEN l.APTT IS NOT NULL AND l.PT IS NOT NULL THEN l.APTT - l.PT END) AS avg_aptt_minus_pt
    FROM Patient AS p
    JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID
    GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX
),
sex_averages AS (
    SELECT
        SEX,
        AVG(avg_alb_minus_tp) AS avg_alb_minus_tp,
        AVG(avg_aptt_minus_pt) AS avg_aptt_minus_pt
    FROM patient_averages
    GROUP BY SEX
),
selected_sexes AS (
    SELECT *
    FROM sex_averages
    WHERE avg_aptt_minus_pt > (SELECT AVG(avg_aptt_minus_pt) FROM sex_averages)
)
SELECT
    AVG(avg_alb_minus_tp) AS avg_alb_minus_tp,
    AVG(avg_aptt_minus_pt) AS avg_aptt_minus_pt,
    AVG(avg_aptt_minus_pt) - (SELECT AVG(avg_aptt_minus_pt) FROM sex_averages) AS avg_excess_aptt_minus_pt
FROM selected_sexes;

d.request: What is the mean, across sexes whose average patient-level APTT − PT is above the mean of the sex-level averages, of (1) the sex-level average patient-level ALB − TP, (2) the sex-level average patient-level APTT − PT, and (3) the amount by which (2) exceeds the mean of all sex-level APTT − PT averages? Link lab records to patients by ID and drop unmatched lab records. For each patient and SEX, first average the per-test ALB − TP and APTT − PT differences, then average those patient-level figures within each SEX, treating each blank or missing SEX value as its own group. Ignore missing values and do not round. Return a single row.
d.sql:
WITH patient_averages AS (
  SELECT p.ID, p.SEX,
         AVG(CASE WHEN l.ALB IS NOT NULL AND l.TP IS NOT NULL THEN l.ALB - l.TP END) AS patient_alb_minus_tp,
         AVG(CASE WHEN l.APTT IS NOT NULL AND l.PT IS NOT NULL THEN l.APTT - l.PT END) AS patient_aptt_minus_pt
  FROM Patient AS p
  JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID
  GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX
),
sex_averages AS (
  SELECT SEX,
         AVG(patient_alb_minus_tp) AS avg_patient_alb_minus_tp,
         AVG(patient_aptt_minus_pt) AS avg_patient_aptt_minus_pt
  FROM patient_averages
  GROUP BY SEX
),
mean_aptt AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_patient_aptt_minus_pt) AS mean_sex_aptt_minus_pt
  FROM sex_averages
)
SELECT AVG(s.avg_patient_alb_minus_tp) AS mean_sex_avg_patient_alb_minus_tp,
       AVG(s.avg_patient_aptt_minus_pt) AS mean_sex_avg_patient_aptt_minus_pt,
       AVG(s.avg_patient_aptt_minus_pt - m.mean_sex_aptt_minus_pt) AS mean_excess_over_sex_mean
FROM sex_averages AS s
CROSS JOIN mean_aptt AS m
WHERE s.avg_patient_aptt_minus_pt > m.mean_sex_aptt_minus_pt
